findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.

Ensure to purchase a regular bottle of bleach. Also, be sure that it has an EPA registration number and is approved to effectively kill norovirus. findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: Both hand-sinks in the kitchen and dish areas lacked hot water. The knobs at the hand-sinks appear to be broken, which is preventing hot water availability at the sinks. Ensure that all hand sinks are provided with hot water to be sure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on October 5, 2026 to see that sinks are repaired.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
At least two of the employees working at the time of inspection could not show proof of food handler certificates. Ensure that all employees who handle food or clean dishes are food handler certified if not food manager certified. Be sure that all certificates are printed out for future inspections. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were several insect glue traps that contained at least 15 dead roaches throughout the facility. There weren’t any live roaches found, however, each of the glue traps contained many dead insects. The facility contracts with Bacon’s Termite & Pest Control as their pest provider. The owner mentioned that the traps are old and have not been replaced in several months. Ensure that the premise is free of insects (live or dead) and to monitor the presence of insects through trapping devices and keeping the facility clean. Will follow-up on April 27, 2026 to check on the replacement of traps.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.

Ensure to purchase wrapped straws or place the unwrapped behind the counter where they are controlled by employees.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There was an egg shell observed in the kitchen’s hand-sink. Discussed with person-in-charge (PIC) and the shell was discarded. Ensure that hand-sinks are only used for handwashing purposes and never food prep or as a dump sink.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were several sliced deli meats that lacked date marking inside of the kitchen prep cooler. Discussed proper date marking with the PIC and date marking labels were provided to the food items. Ensure that all sliced deli meats are date marked if being held in house longer than 24 hours. Be sure to discard if seven days are exceeded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: There was a spray bottle of a cleaning chemical stored on the bottom shelf of the prep table. There was also single service items and equipment used for cooking stored on the shelf. Discussed with PIC and the bottle was moved to the storage area where other hazardous chemicals are stored. Ensure that hazardous chemicals are never stored with food or items that will come in contact with food to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Cooked tater tots were observed at room temperature and was tempted at 94F. Discussed with PIC that cooked potatoes are considered TCS (time/temperature control for safety) and will need to be hot held. PIC placed tater tots and fries under a heat lamp to correct the violation. Be sure that TCS foods are maintained at 135F or above to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed

Observed PIC not wash hands before engaging in food preparation. PIC shook inspector’s hand and proceeded to prepare food. Discussed with PIC to wash hands before engaging in food production. Ensure that hands are washed before engaging in food production after switching tasks. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Observed PIC using bare hands to touch a ready-to-eat food item. PIC mentioned that the facility just received boxes of gloves prior to inspector’s arrival. Ensure that employees do not use  bare hand contact with RTE foods. 

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

The freezer is used to store ice for the drinks in the bar area. Ensure that equipment of food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained as frequent as necessary to prevent contamination.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several food items not to be date marked in a prep cooler in the kitchen area. These items include but aren't limited to deli meats, cheeses, and salads. PIC discarded some food items and the others were date marked with the appropriate opening date. Ensure that TCS foods that are held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parmesan).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of bleach to be stored on a shelf mixed with single service items. Discussed with PIC and bottle of bleach was removed. Ensure that chemicals are always stored separate from single service items in order to prevent contamination.  

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Observed clean utensils stored in a container with food debris at the bottom. Discussed with PIC and container was switched. Ensure that utensils are always stored in manner that prevents them from contamination. 

4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
Observed the handwashing sink in the dish machine area to not have an adequate flow of hot water. PIC mentioned that the hand-sink barely gets used. Ensure that hand-sinks always have an adequate flow of hot water to properly wash hands. 

5-103.12: Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water (A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

Overall, the facility is need of a deep cleaning. 
- floors, walls, sides and underneath of equipment are soiled with food debris and splatter. 
- Shelving in the kitchen area has food debris
- Wall behind dish machine (mold on caulk where dish machine and wall meet)
Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris.  

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Observed  improper hand washing technique. See that hand washing technique is revisited with staff. Use a barrier to turn off the faucet - do not recontaminate hands by touching soiled faucet. Educated staff on hand washing during inspection.

 (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: observed ham in the preparation cooler to not be properly date marked. See that applicable foods are date marked and used within seven days. Marked during inspection.

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19:  The reach-in freezer at the cafe is coated with ice and frost. A spilled ice bag has been frozen to the base. The kitchen staff are using only the ice from a bag within the freezer. The unit should be defrosted during winter break - it has to be turned off and brought to the alley to thaw. See that ice is thawed and food is removed from frozen base. 

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1) Counter under microwave was soiled with food debris/general buildup.
2) Base of waffle iron and baking sheet beneath were soiled with food debris.
Clean under equipment and general surfaces daily/as needed.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC still needs to take a food allergen course for certification and noted they plan to complete allergen certification later today. Ensure certified food managers complete food allergen certification before next routine inspection, and maintain copies of allergen certifications along with all other certifications for staff on-site.
All certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority items were observed for reheating, sanitization, and proper disposal of waste water. A cooler with an iced up condensing unit was being used for cold holding but observed holding at 51F during inspection. PIC did not have employee health documentation and copies of certifications were not available for staff. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection in 2 weeks.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents were not available at the time of inspection. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. Reporting agreements were signed by staff during inspection. Ensure all staff are educated on employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
301.11 Soap was not available at the dish room handwashing sink. Soap was provided.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:

A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 While discussing ware washing process in the dish room, the cook began to use the wall mounted chemical dispenser to fill the sanitize basin. Inspector advised the chemical jug for sanitizer was empty. Cook was unaware the product was empty. Quat tablets were used to prepare sanitizer solution. Ensure concentration of 200-400ppm as required by instructions on manufacturer’s label and a contact time of at least 30 seconds on all surfaces prior to air drying.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 (B) Inside microwave was soiled with food splash, some of which appeared encrusted from previous operating days. Clean the microwave as needed to eliminate buildup.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 Gravy and cheese sauce out on prep table were observed with internal temperatures of 78F and 83F respectively. Products were said to be held in he prep cooler overnight and just pulled recently to reheat. PIC briefly placed pans in the tabletop warmer but were removed by the cook to reheat products in the microwave some time prior to inspector’s arrival. Cheese sauce and gravy were reheated above 165F prior to hot holding. Ensure foods are left in the cooler until time to reheat. Use equipment intended for reheating to quickly and properly reheat TCS foods. 
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly so the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Reach-in cooler in kitchen was observed with heavy ice accumulation at the ceiling condensing unit. The hanging thermometer was reading near 50F. Frozen foods (fries, potatoes, tater tots) had internal temperatures at 32F-41F depending on how long they were in the cooler, and bacon pulled from the freezer to thaw overnight was observed with an internal temperature of 39F. Other foods included heads of lettuce and a whole whole tomato. All foods were relocated to coolers holding at 40F/below. Cooler door was kept closed for over 30 minutes and temperature was confirmed at 51F. Cooler will not be used until it is serviced and able to maintain temperature. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 1) Counter under microwave was soiled with food debris/general buildup.
2) Base of waffle iron and baking sheet beneath were soiled with food debris.
Clean under equipment and general surfaces daily/as needed.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Old, dirty mop water was observed in the mop bucket by the mop sink in the dish room. Cook noted they mopped the day prior. PIC discarded the mop water during inspection. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave sitting in the facility overnight, as waste water can serve as a potential water/food source for pests.
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for staff. Server completed training through previous employer and was advised to check with them about getting a copy. If copy cannot be obtained then server needs to complete another food handler course for certification. Cook has a food manager certification, but copy of certification was not available. Ensure copies of all food handler and manager certifications are available and maintained on-site by next routine inspection.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 PIC has not completed food allergen certification. Certification needs to be completed by next routine inspection. Maintain a copy of allergen certification along with all other certifications for staff on-site.
All certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.comment:

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at the dish area hand sink. Paper towels and soap mush be provided at all hand sinks. Paper towels were stocked during the inspection. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed multiple items in the prep cooler to not be properly date marked with a 7 day date marking. Additionally, there was yogurt observed past the manufacturer’s date marking. Ensure all TCS foods are clearly marked with a date marking. Items past the manufacturers date marking were discarded. The items were prepped a few days ago and were date marked accordingly to correct the violation.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed no sani bucket being used during the inspection. Sanitizer must be available during all hours of operation. Ensure sani buckets are made before food prep begins. A sani bucket was made during the inspection.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed mops stored in the mop bucket with old mop water inside the bucket. Mops must be stored in a position that allows them to air dry properly, and mop water must be discarded after use. 
  
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.comment:

findings.comment:
4-904.11: Observed clean utensils in the dish area to be stored with the food contact surface facing upward. Ensure utensils are inverted so the food contact surface is not touched by employees hands. 
(A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.comment:
